clue.text: Sirens chant quietly close to Odysseus

parts.note: a mantra is a chant repeated in meditation
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of the hero's name is wanted

parts.note: the hero's name ends in this letter

explanation.surface: The Sirens of myth sing softly to lure Odysseus as he sails past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sirens' is read as the mythical singers, but here it means women who lure men in.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman, and a mantrap is slang for exactly such a dangerously alluring woman.

clue.text: American blocking British politician's plans

indicators.note: something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Members of Parliament, British politicians
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: An American is obstructing the plans of a British politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British politician's' looks possessive but is read as MPs, the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Maps are plans, as in a street plan or a floor plan drawn of an area.

clue.text: Root for the Scottish groom turning up with no ring at first

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top
with no says that letter must be left out

parts.note: to preen is to groom oneself

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the initial letter of ring

explanation.surface: A Scottish bridegroom is cheered on as he arrives without a wedding ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Root for' looks like cheering on; it is 'a root' in the Scots language. The reversed word loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Neep is the Scots word for a turnip or swede, a root vegetable.

clue.text: Finally remember to feed the forlorn pet hamster?

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of each word that follows

parts.words: remember to feed the forlorn pet
parts.note: the final letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: A reminder at last to feed the sad pet hamster.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that the definition is an example: a hamster is one kind of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamster is a small gnawing mammal, one example of the rodent order.

clue.text: Something that spans a couple of games of cards

wordplay.words: a couple of games of cards
wordplay.note: two card games: one like blackjack, and the partnership bidding game

explanation.surface: A session covering two card games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spans' suggests a period of time covering the games; it is a structure crossing water. Pontoon is the British name for blackjack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontoon bridge is a temporary bridge laid on floating pontoons, so it spans a river.

clue.text: Divine drink before noon with Ms Hayworth?

parts.note: a.m. means before midday
Rita Hayworth, the Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: A heavenly cocktail taken in the morning with the film star Rita Hayworth.
explanation.definitionFit: Amrita is the nectar of immortality drunk by the gods in Hindu mythology.

clue.text: It's my fault maiden heard you entering palace complex

indicators.note: entering means these letters go inside the following word
complex means intricate and tangled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: M is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound, as a single letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter sounds like this pronoun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A confession of blame after a maiden was overheard inside a palace complex.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for 'through my fault', an admission of one's own error.

clue.text: Provocative couple on vacation breaking local record

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a local is a British pub, the one nearest home

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its middle so only its outside letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters of couple
a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: A provocative pair on holiday break a local record.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters of the pub word go before the inserted pair, the last after.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiary means inflammatory, tending to stir up conflict, so provocative.

clue.text: In charge of theatres in Barking

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, and mad letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone running the theatres in Barking, the East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of East London, but here it is slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding the reins means steering a horse, so the idiom means being in control.

clue.text: Spy me messily eating noodles incognito

definitions.note: used as a noun: an assumed identity

indicators.note: something eating takes another thing inside it
done messily means done untidily, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
udon are thick Japanese wheat noodles

explanation.surface: A spy sloppily eats noodles while working undercover.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym is a false name, an incognito being a disguised or assumed identity.

clue.text: Caged men lift rocks, enthralling the setter in attractive region

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the letters hold another piece inside
a thing on the rocks is wrecked, so these letters are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the setter refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Imprisoned men lifting rocks hold the crossword setter captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' looks like what the prisoners lift, but it is a verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic field is the area around a magnet where its attracting force acts.

clue.text: A drunk's caught interrupting meetings here

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: interrupting means cutting into the middle, so a letter breaks into the word

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A drunk is arrested for disrupting meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse, and race days there are called meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous Berkshire racecourse that hosts race meetings, notably Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Renouncing converts, church in conflict

indicators.note: to convert is to change form, so these letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Converts renouncing their faith leave the church in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converts' looks like a noun for new believers; it is a verb acting on the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Incongruence is a lack of agreement or harmony between things, a state of conflict.

clue.text: On time, teacher eats and leaves

parts.note: rabbi means teacher in Hebrew
T is the abbreviation for time
eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: A punctual teacher eats lunch and then goes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the teacher above the time. 'Leaves' looks like a verb; it is lettuce and salad greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit food is a dismissive informal name for salad, lettuce leaves and raw greens.

clue.text: Silence fills Glaswegian flat after opening fight

indicators.note: to fill something is to go inside it
after the opening means once the first letter has gone

parts.note: a tenement is a flat in a large shared block, typical of Glasgow
to gag someone is to silence them

explanation.surface: A gagging order is imposed on a Glasgow flat once a fight breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: Tenement flats are the classic Glasgow housing; the word loses its T before the gag goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a military battle or clash between opposing forces, so a fight.

clue.text: Cow kicking dead relative

indicators.note: kicking a habit means giving it up, so a letter is given up here

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate
d is the abbreviation for dead

explanation.surface: A cow kicks a dead relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like the animal, or even an insult for the relative; it is a verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a family member, the sister of one's parent.

clue.text: Unlimited rent increase holding back sandwich-maker's business

indicators.note: holding means keeping something within, so a piece sits inside
without its limits a word loses its two end letters, keeping only the middle

parts.note: the middle two letters of rent

indicators.note: back means the company name is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Pret a Manger is a British sandwich chain
a rise is an increase

explanation.surface: An unchecked rent rise is holding back a sandwich shop's trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwich-maker' suggests the Earl of Sandwich; it is Pret a Manger, the British sandwich chain.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a business or company, a commercial undertaking.

clue.text: Pressing ahead after leader quits in support of extremists in Kazakhstan

indicators.note: when the leader quits, the word loses its first letter
the extremes of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the country
a side ahead in a match is leading

explanation.surface: A leader quits in Kazakhstan while urgent action goes ahead in support of extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'in support of' puts the trimmed word below the two letters from Kazakhstan.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working dough by pressing and folding it with the hands.

clue.text: Lots of smart people leaving Britain and Germany amid downpours

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for Britain or British
rain falling heavily, the first downpour
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
the second downpour

explanation.surface: Talented people quit Britain and Germany to escape the endless rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downpours' is plural, so it gives the same word twice, and the two country letters sit amid them.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain drain is the emigration of highly educated or skilled people from a country.

clue.text: After abandoning children, pull singer

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so letters are dropped

parts.note: to wrench is to pull violently
ch is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: After deserting the kids, someone tugs at a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is crossword shorthand for a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wren is a tiny songbird, and birds are often called singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Oddly, booze fails to inspire King of the North

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the letters take another inside
oddly picks out the letters in odd-numbered places

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Drink fails to rouse the King of the North, as in a fantasy saga.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King of the North' reads as one title, but the definition starts at 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreal means northern, from Boreas, the Greek god of the north wind.

clue.text: Where you go when you're out for the night?

definitions.text: Where you go when you're out for the night?

parts.words: Where you go when you're out for the night?
parts.note: surface reading: a venue for a night out on the town
setter's reading: out cold, fast asleep until morning

explanation.walkthrough: 'Out for the night' suggests partying, but here it means unconscious with sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jocular idiom for sleep, from Nod, the land Cain was exiled to in Genesis.

clue.text: Somewhat nasty eye infection

indicators.note: somewhat means only a part, so the letters are a portion of the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the whole second

explanation.surface: A rather unpleasant infection of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter lets 'eye' do double duty: it ends the hidden letters and also belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid caused by a bacterial infection.

clue.text: Hebridean island's peak is covered in ice

indicators.note: a covered top is hidden from view, so the uppermost letter disappears

parts.note: Islay is an island of the Inner Hebrides, famous for whisky
the top letter of the down entry, its first

explanation.surface: A Scottish island's mountain summit is coated in ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' looks like frozen water but is slang for kill. In a down clue the peak is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ice someone is American slang for murdering them, and to slay is to kill.

clue.text: Periodically comb priest for daggers

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: second and fourth letters
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel

explanation.surface: Someone combs a priest's hair from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daggers' means the printer's mark, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelus is the dagger symbol used in printing to mark footnotes; obeli is the plural.

clue.text: Basic large English blokes tucking into meatballs regularly

indicators.note: tucking into food means eating it, taking it inside
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
blokes is British slang for men
E is the abbreviation for English
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Big English lads tuck into a plate of meatballs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or essential, relating to first principles, so basic.

clue.text: Senility caused by party drug without label

parts.note: a do is an informal British word for a party
a tag is a label
E for ecstasy, set outside the label

explanation.surface: Dementia brought on by an unmarked pill at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside: the drug letter stands beyond the label rather than missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the feeble mental state of old age, a period of senility.

clue.text: Surprisingly ready to accept leaderless cult's extra-marital relations

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the letters take another piece inside
something turning out surprisingly is not as expected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaderless means without its head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A leaderless cult is surprisingly willing to accept affairs outside marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is sexual relations between a married person and someone other than their spouse.
